title: ingestion/pipeline: per-line String allocation for case-insensitive header scan
description:
## Why this issue exists

Three header-scanning functions allocate heap Strings on every line of every article just to do a case-insensitive ASCII prefix comparison. On the hot article ingestion path this produces unnecessary GC pressure.

## What needs to be done

### has_header (ingestion.rs:308-327)

Called 5 times per article (once per mandatory header). For each call, every line in the header section is processed as:
  `String::from_utf8_lossy(line).to_ascii_lowercase()`
That produces a Cow allocation (always heap when replacements occur) plus a second String for the lowercase result. The correct fix is a byte-level case-insensitive prefix check:
  `line.len() >= needle.len() && line[..needle.len()].eq_ignore_ascii_case(needle.as_bytes())`
No allocation needed.

### prepend_path_header (ingestion.rs:285-286)

Same pattern: `String::from_utf8_lossy(trimmed).to_ascii_lowercase()` called on every non-body line to check for the 'Path:' prefix. A direct `trimmed.len() >= 5 && trimmed[..5].eq_ignore_ascii_case(b"path:")` check requires no allocation.

### parse_message_id_and_newsgroups (pipeline.rs:538)

`s.to_ascii_lowercase()` allocates a String per header line to do two prefix checks. The same byte-level approach removes the allocation entirely.

All three are on the article ingestion hot path and the fix in each case is a one-line change from `to_ascii_lowercase()` to `eq_ignore_ascii_case`.
